public_rationale: The retrieved independent estimate points against a 70% share of the global compute base, but it concerns late-2025 operational capacity. It does not directly settle the claim about demand in Q1 2026. Treating it as a decisive contradiction would change both the period and the measure. No matching worldwide demand estimate was found.
limitations: The source leaves the demand measure and observation period unspecified.
The strongest counterevidence is explicitly tentative and outside the target period.
An unresolved result does not validate the asserted minimum.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic and OpenAI together account for at least 70%, and possibly 80-90%, of all AI compute demand.

statement.excerpt: Between them, Anthropic and OpenAI represent the vast majority of all AI compute demand — at a minimum 70%, if not 80% to 90%.

our_interpretation: The firm minimum is 70%; 80% to 90% is a suggested higher range.
The ordinary reading covers worldwide AI compute demand, including training, inference, and internal AI workloads, rather than only frontier-model cloud rentals.
For this ongoing observation, I use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that public reporting could cover before the June 8 post.
Compute demand should be attributed to the workload or customer using it, avoiding double-counting the cloud provider and its customer.
The claim is a compute-share claim, so metric_scope is null. Spending can be a proxy only if numerator and denominator use comparable prices, scope, and periods.
Installed capacity, ownership, utilization, incremental purchases, and demand are distinct measures.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive, period-matched measurement establishes that Anthropic and OpenAI jointly account for at least 70% of worldwide AI compute demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive, period-matched measurement, or a defensible bound, places their combined share below 70%.
